subject: Biology
description: Reproductive system, fertilization, hormones, gestation, twins

questions.stem: FERTILIZATION (egg + sperm union) in humans normally occurs in the:
questions.explanation: Fertilization — usually in the AMPULLA (widest part) of the FALLOPIAN TUBE (also called oviduct), within ~24 hours of ovulation (egg released from ovary). Sperm swims through cervix → uterus → fallopian tube. Of ~300 million sperm, only ~200 reach egg; only 1 fuses. Resulting ZYGOTE travels down tube to UTERUS over ~6-7 days; implants in uterine wall (endometrium) → embryo development. ECTOPIC pregnancy = implantation in tube (medical emergency).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Normal human GESTATION period (from fertilization to birth) is approximately:
questions.explanation: Gestation: ~266 days (~38 weeks) from FERTILIZATION; ~280 days (~40 weeks) from LAST MENSTRUAL PERIOD (LMP) — the standard medical reference for due date estimation (since exact fertilization date is rarely known). 'Term' delivery: 37-42 weeks. PRETERM = <37 weeks; POST-TERM = >42 weeks. Distractor 1 = 9 months ≈ 270 days, casual count from LMP. Distractor 3 = postdates. Distractor 4 = elephant gestation, not human.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The hormone that maintains pregnancy by SUPPORTING the uterine lining is:
questions.explanation: PROGESTERONE (= 'pro-gestation') — secreted by corpus luteum (post-ovulation), then by PLACENTA after ~10 weeks. Maintains endometrium (uterine lining), prevents menstruation, suppresses uterine contractions until full term, prepares mammary glands. Drop in progesterone triggers LABOUR. ESTROGEN — develops female secondary characteristics; with progesterone in menstrual cycle. PROGESTERONE-only contraceptive pills work by preventing ovulation. RU-486 (mifepristone) — anti-progesterone; used for medical abortion.

options.option_text: Two eggs are fertilized by two sperm
One zygote splits into two embryos
Two sperm fertilize a single egg
Two embryos fuse together in womb

questions.explanation: MONOZYGOTIC (identical) twins — ONE zygote (one egg + one sperm) splits into two embryos in early development. Same DNA, same sex, often same blood type. ~3-4 per 1000 births. DIZYGOTIC (fraternal) twins — TWO eggs released, each fertilized by DIFFERENT sperm. Different DNA (like normal siblings born together), can be different sexes. Frequency varies by ethnicity + maternal age (~10-30 per 1000). Hormonal IVF treatments increase fraternal twin rate. Distractor 3 = polyspermy (usually fatal). Distractor 4 = chimaerism (rare).

questions.stem: The female reproductive HORMONE primarily produced by the ovaries' GRAAFIAN follicle is:

options.option_text: FSH, by the anterior pituitary gland
LH, by the anterior pituitary gland

questions.explanation: GRAAFIAN FOLLICLE = mature ovarian follicle containing the egg; secretes ESTROGEN as it grows under FSH stimulation. After ovulation, the ruptured follicle becomes CORPUS LUTEUM, which secretes PROGESTERONE. Cycle hormones: FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone — pituitary) starts follicle growth; estrogen rises; LH (Luteinising Hormone) surge triggers OVULATION (~day 14); corpus luteum secretes progesterone (luteal phase). If no fertilization → corpus luteum degenerates → menstruation.

questions.stem: The number of CHROMOSOMES in a human SPERM cell is:
questions.explanation: Normal HUMAN body cells (somatic) = DIPLOID (2n) = 46 chromosomes (22 autosome pairs + 1 sex chromosome pair). GAMETES (sperm + egg) = HAPLOID (n) = 23 chromosomes — produced via MEIOSIS. Sperm carries 22 autosomes + either X (→ daughter) or Y (→ son). Egg always carries 22 autosomes + X. Father determines child's sex. Fertilization restores diploid (23+23 = 46) zygote. Distractor 1 = somatic-cell count. Distractor 3 = polyploid, not normal. Distractor 4 = autosomes alone in sperm.

questions.stem: The PLACENTA is a temporary organ that:

options.option_text: Stores extra amniotic fluid for the foetus
Allows nutrient/gas exchange between mother and foetus
Produces only milk for after the delivery
Serves as the foetus' main brain region area

questions.explanation: PLACENTA — temporary organ formed from foetal + maternal tissue. Functions: (1) NUTRITION — passes glucose, amino acids, vitamins from mother to foetus; (2) RESPIRATION — O₂ in, CO₂ out via diffusion; (3) EXCRETION — foetal wastes to mother; (4) HORMONE production — hCG (basis of pregnancy tests), progesterone, estrogen, hPL; (5) BARRIER — keeps mother + foetus's blood SEPARATE (different blood types possible) but allows exchange. Some toxins, drugs, viruses can cross (smoking, alcohol, Zika, HIV). DELIVERED as 'AFTERBIRTH' after baby. Distractor 1 = amnion role.
